core_obligations: Reduce to modules on the small Zariski site by identifying O_S-modules on S with modules on the ringed site of the Zariski topology (proof lines 2693-2694).

Identify the functor F to F^a with pullback along the morphism of ringed sites comparing the Zariski topology with the topology in question, and identify the corresponding pushforward with restriction along the inclusion (proof lines 2695-2702).

Deduce that the composite of the pushforward with the pullback returns the original quasi-coherent module, so that the adjunction unit is an isomorphism on quasi-coherent modules (proof lines 2703-2705).

Compute the Hom sets: the Hom set between two associated modules is the Hom set between the two pulled back modules, which by adjunction is the Hom set between the original module and the composite, which the previous step identifies with the Hom set between the two original modules, giving full faithfulness (proof lines 2706-2712).
proof_roadmap: Identify with modules on the small Zariski site (proof lines 2693-2694).
Present the functor as a pullback along a morphism of ringed sites (proof lines 2695-2702).
The composite with its right adjoint is the identity on quasi-coherent modules (proof lines 2703-2705).
Conclude by the adjunction computation on Hom sets (proof lines 2706-2712).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme S and a topology among Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic and fppf, the lemma states that each of the functors sending a quasi-coherent module to the associated module on the big site or the small site of that topology is fully faithful (statement lines 2675-2688). The proof identifies the functor with a pullback along a morphism of ringed sites, observes that its right adjoint is restriction along the inclusion of the small Zariski site into the site in question, and then computes the induced map on Hom sets through the adjunction: the right adjoint followed by the left adjoint returns the original quasi-coherent module, which turns the string of identifications of Hom sets into the identity on Hom sets of quasi-coherent modules on S, giving full faithfulness (proof lines 2690-2712). The claim is H2: the argument is short but it is a complete derivation, consisting of an identification of the functor with a pullback, an identification of its right adjoint, and a chain of adjunction identifications that has to be written out correctly.
